name: Invoice Ninja
tagline: Invoicing, quotes, payments, expenses, and client portal software

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Pro listed at $14/month or $140/year.
pricing.freeTier: The free plan covers up to 5 clients with unlimited invoicing.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Up to 5 clients, unlimited invoices and 4 invoice templates.

tiers.name: Ninja Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited clients/invoices, 11 templates and up to 10 interlinked companies per login.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: 1–2 users at the starting price; scales to 51–100 users at $300/month or $250/month annual equivalent; 250 PEPPOL credits included.
tiers.notes: Annual billing gives 2 months free; price scales by account-user band.

tiers.name: Premium Business
tiers.limits: Up to 100 users plus migration, custom reports and developer concierge.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 5 clients, unlimited invoices and 4 invoice templates.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (2 months free); annual charged as one yearly payment; 30-day money-back promise
pricing.hiddenCosts: Payment-gateway processing fees are separate. Enterprise prices rise with user count, from $18/month for 1–2 users to $300/month for 51–100; only 250 PEPPOL credits are included and extra-credit pricing was not public.

verdictSummary: Invoice Ninja is open source, so the hosted subscription can be replaced by self-hosting if you can handle ops, updates, payment config, and backups.
coreLoopDIY: Self-host Invoice Ninja or build a simpler invoice generator with clients, line items, PDF export, and payment links.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because billing software is boring and should not break on invoice day.

priorArt.name: Invoice Ninja
priorArt.desc: The product's own open-source invoicing platform.

alternatives.name: Invoice Ninja self-hosted
alternatives.desc: The same invoicing stack on your own server; billing is free, the license is source-available, and removing its branding costs extra.

facts.install: Official Docker Compose/INmanage path, or a PHP web-server installation with a MySQL-compatible database
facts.dataFormat: Clients, invoices, quotes, expenses, payments, and settings live in the deployment's MySQL-compatible database; uploaded documents and generated files live under the persistent storage directory, and APP_KEY protects selected secrets.
facts.gapVsPaid: The application is familiar, but the free self-hosted edition transfers uptime, security, mail delivery, backups, upgrades, and branding removal from Invoice Ninja's service to the user.
facts.setupBlocker: The free path requires PHP or Docker, MySQL, cron and queue workers, TLS, mail, backups, upgrades, and accepting Invoice Ninja branding unless a separate white-label license is purchased.

alternatives.name: InvoiceShelf
alternatives.desc: Invoices, estimates, expenses, payments and a client portal; the bill arrives as Docker maintenance instead.

facts.install: Deploy a stable tagged release with the official Docker Compose example
facts.dataFormat: Invoices, estimates, customers, expenses, payments, and settings live in the configured application database, SQLite is available for a small install, with uploaded files in persistent server storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: InvoiceShelf has a smaller payment-gateway, mobile-app, integration, recurring-billing, and support ecosystem than Invoice Ninja, with a less mature current release line.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is choosing a stable 2.x release rather than the default next/3.x alpha branch, then operating Docker, persistent storage, mail, HTTPS, backups, and upgrades.

alternatives.name: ERPNext
alternatives.desc: Quotes, invoices, payments, expenses and a portal inside a much larger ERP than anyone ordered.

facts.install: Managed Frappe Cloud signup, or the supported Frappe Docker/Bench deployment
facts.dataFormat: Self-hosted companies live in MariaDB site databases with site files and attachments on the server; managed-hosting data lives in the selected Frappe Cloud site.
facts.gapVsPaid: ERPNext can issue and collect invoices but its much larger ERP interface is less polished for client portals, payment gateways, recurring billing, and solo-business onboarding.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting is an ERP deployment rather than a desktop install: Docker or Bench, MariaDB, Redis, workers, a reverse proxy, backups, upgrades, and country-specific accounting setup.

alternatives.name: Zoho Invoice
alternatives.desc: Quotes, time, expenses, payments and a portal for free; Zoho still keeps an annual invoice ceiling.

facts.install: Hosted signup or the official mobile/desktop app
facts.dataFormat: Customers, projects, time, expenses, estimates, invoices, payment records, and portal data live in Zoho's cloud; exports and account backups are available.
facts.gapVsPaid: Zoho Invoice is easier to adopt but the free service caps annual invoices, users, and projects and retains Zoho branding, making it less flexible than a paid Invoice Ninja account.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Crater
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Still widely recommended; last push August 2024 and the last release is four years old.

rejectedAlternatives.name: InvoicePlane
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Quotes, invoices and payments are solid; expenses and a real client portal never show up.

rejectedAlternatives.name: SolidInvoice
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Quotes, recurring invoices and payments are here; expense tracking and a client portal are not.

notes: Clean hosted-open-source yes, with a realistic ops caveat.
prompt:
Build me a small invoicing app to replace hosted Invoice Ninja. Requirements:

- Note in the README that Invoice Ninja itself is open source and self-hostable;
  this build is the lighter option for someone who needs invoices, not a platform.
- Node + Express + better-sqlite3, admin UI on localhost:4840, server-rendered pages.
- Clients (name, email, address, currency, default rate) and invoices with line items
  (description, qty, unit price, tax %), auto-numbered INV-2026-001 style.
- Generate a clean PDF per invoice with puppeteer from an HTML template: my logo,
  payment terms, and bank details read from a config file.
- Email the PDF to the client via SMTP (creds in .env); track draft/sent/paid status
  and show a dashboard of unpaid invoices with days outstanding.
- Optional Stripe payment link per invoice (key in .env), included in the PDF and
  the email. I mark invoices paid by hand when money lands.
- Nightly backup: copy the SQLite file to backups/YYYY-MM-DD.db, keep 30.
- Binds to localhost, no client portal, no accounts, no telemetry.
- Out of scope: quotes, expenses, multi-user, and automatic payment reconciliation.
- README: .env keys, how to edit the invoice template, and the numbering rule.
